Rules o f Procedure for t he Data Protection Supervisory Authority adopted by ESA Council on 13 June 2017 12. Deliberation and decisions After closure of the written procedure or, as the case may be, of the hearing, the Supervisory Authority shall deliberate on its decision. The delib erations of the Supervisory Authority shall be held out of the presence of either party or of any other person. Before issuing a decision, the Supervisory Authority may propose to parties amicable resolution or settlement. The decisions of the Supervisory Authority shall: - be taken by majority; - state the grounds on which the Supervisory Authority's decisions are based ; - contain findings which cover the main facts and legal arguments put forward by the two parties; - state the names of the members o f the Supervisory Authority who took part in the deliberations; - be signed by the chairman of the Supervisory Authority and the registrar; - indicate the date of the decision; - be sent to the Director General, the Data Protection Officer and to the complainant , in copies certified true by the registrar, within thirty days of being delivered or, where this time limit of thirty days cannot be respected, in the timeframe authoris

fficer and to the complainant , in copies certified true by the registrar, within thirty days of being delivered or, where this time limit of thirty days cannot be respected, in the timeframe authorised by the chairman; - may also be communicated to any person upon request, u nless otherwise the S upervisory Authority so decides ; the Supervisory Authority may decide that a decision shall only be communicated with the name of the claimant or any other person mentioned therein deleted. The Supervisory Authority may award financia l compensation to the claimant within the limit of 10, 000 Euro. The d ecision s of the Supervisory Authority shall be final and binding on both parties; no appeal is possible against them . 13. Costs The proceedings before the Supervisory Authority shall be fr ee of charge. The Agency shall in all cases pay its own costs. Any costs incurred by the claimant in the course of the proceedings, in particular fees payable to a person chosen from outside the Agency to represent or assist him /her , shall be borne by hi m /her , unless the Supervisory Authority decides otherwise. ncil on 13 June 2017 14. Review The Supervisory Authority may be asked by the parties to: - interpret a decision, should difficulties arise as to the m eaning or scope of the decision ; - review a decision if a fact of decisive importance comes to the knowledge of the Supervisory Authority and of one of the parties after the pronouncement of such a decision ; nevertheless, no request for review may be made after the expiry of a period of three months following the discove ry of the fact mentioned above and - in any case - five years after the date of the decision. The period of three months shall not apply if the claimant was unable for valid reasons to make the request. Any request for interpretation or review shall be s ubmitted to the chairman of the Supervisory authority who may deliver a reasoned decision stating the request to be inadmissible, if (i) he /her considers that this request clearly amounts to an appeal against a decision of the Supervisory Authority and (i i) none of the members of the Supervisory Authority who would be called upon to deal with the matter objects in writing. There shall be no appeal against this decision. Subject to the above provision, the procedure for review shall commence with a decision of the Supervisory Authority formally declaring that a new fact exists, that it is of a character which justifies the review, and that the request for rev

ure for review shall commence with a decision of the Supervisory Authority formally declaring that a new fact exists, that it is of a character which justifies the review, and that the request for review is admissible for that reason . Clerical and arithmetical mistakes in the decision, or any accidental error or omission, may be corrected by the Supervisory Authority, either on its own initiative or on the application of either party. Policy o n Personal Data Protection adopted by Director General of ESA on 1 March 2022 III. POLICY ON PERSONAL DATA PROTECTION ( adopted by Director General of ESA on 1 March 2022 ) 1. INTRODUCTION In the performance of its mission, the Agency collects and Processes certain Personal Data concerning various individuals, in particular Staff Members or Contractor Personnel. These Personal Data may be collected by the Agency or made available to the Agency by the individuals themselves or by third parties, located in several jurisdictions. The Agency, while not being subject to national or international laws on Personal Data protection, wants to ensure a high level of protection of Personal Data and, by doing so, to preserve the dignity and privacy of the concerned individuals. To that eff ect, Council adopted, on 13 June 2017, the Resolution on a “Personal Data Protection Policy” (ESA/C/CCLXVIII/Res.2 (Final)) setting forth the principles of Persona

e concerned individuals. To that eff ect, Council adopted, on 13 June 2017, the Resolution on a “Personal Data Protection Policy” (ESA/C/CCLXVIII/Res.2 (Final)) setting forth the principles of Personal Data Protection at ESA and mandating the Director General to adopt a Policy on Personal Dat a Protection (“Policy”) implementing the said principles and establishing an appropriate governance scheme, the latter to be composed of an independent Data Protection Supervisory Authority, an internal Data Protection Committee, and a Data Protection Offi cer . 2. POLICY In order to ensure a high level of protection of Personal Data concerning individuals and in particular Agency’s Staff Members and Contractor Personnel, it is the Agency’s policy to: - adopt a structured framework to effectively ensure the pro tection and safeguard of Personal Data Processed or disclosed by, on behalf of, or to the Agency; - increase awareness and responsibility of Staff Members with respect to Personal Data protection; - establish governance, including functions and bodies (e.g. Data Protection Officer, Data Protection Supervisory Authority, Data Protection Committee) and operations necessary for the effectiveness of Personal Data protection. 3. I NTRODUCTION Pursuant to Article XII.1.b of the Convention, the Director General (DG) is the chief executive officer of the Agency, its legal representative, and has authority over the sites of the Agency. In that capacity, the DG has overall responsibility and is accountable for all health and safety risks (i) arising on ESA sites, and/or (ii) arising in the context of the Agency’s activities. The DG has thus responsibility for all persons 1 , irrespective of their status, who participate in the Agency’s activities or are physically present on its sites. What these responsibilities are, and how they should be discharged, depends upon the context, and includes risks to Staff members when on mission and teleworking. Employment is an opportunity for improving the physical and psychological health of manpower resources 2 . As well as benefiting individuals, the Agency will gain through health - related improvement in work performance and reduction in sickness absence. It is therefore in the interest of the Agency that risks to health and safety are identified and subject to constant reduction. Decisions that relate to the Agency’s activities will be motivat

bsence. It is therefore in the interest of the Agency that risks to health and safety are identified and subject to constant reduction. Decisions that relate to the Agency’s activities will be motivated by understanding the associated potential for risks and the measures needed to reduce them. The process of risk assessment provides a mechanism to identify, control and mitigate risks. This policy sets the principles governing the Agency’s risk - based approach and ensures that account is taken of health and safety in the planning and conduct of the 1 F or the purposes of the present policy, “ p ersons ” covers anyone present on an ESA site (including visitors) . 2 F or the purposes of the present policy, “ m anpower resources ” covers staff members and contractor personnel . ESA/ADMIN/IPOL - HESA(20 22 )1 Page 2 ac tivities of the Agency. The policy shall ensure that, at corporate level, an appropriate and consistent approach is taken to identify and control risks. 2. POLICY It is the Agency’s policy to: - Keep as low as reasonably practicable all health and safety risks arising in the context of its activities. - Provide adequate resources to identify and manage risks and to improve continuously standards of health and safety. - Establish a working environment in which its manpower resources and any other individual on site performing temporary assignments (i.e., visiting scie

ve continuously standards of health and safety. - Establish a working environment in which its manpower resources and any other individual on site performing temporary assignments (i.e., visiting scientists, interns etc…) recognise and assume appropriate responsibilities for promoting health and safety at work. - Promote the physical and psychological health of its manpower resources. Maintain a monitoring regime to: - control health and safety risks. - monitor the status of health and safety management. - identify the root causes of incidents and instances of occupational illness. - keep track of changes to national health and safety legislation where ESA sites are located. - anticipate changes to the control of health and safety risks whether internal or external to the Agency. 3. SCOPE OF APPLICATION This policy applies to the activities of the Agency and to any person present on ESA sites (including manpower resources and visitors). It also applies to Staff members when on mission and during teleworking 3 . 4. The Department in charge of procurement The Department in charge of procurement, as the formal interface with the contractor companies, will ensure: a) throughout the tendering process and resulting contract, the necessary provisions are in place to bind contractors to the requirements set by this policy are correctly included b) that the key requirements of ESA’s health and safety policy are described within the contractual document ation In the case of any doubt, it shall seek the advice of the person responsible for providing safety advice at the pertaining establishments. 9. The staff association The staff representatives in charge of health and safety matter s are SAC members, who: a) are selected at local level in each site according to the applicable procedures and who benefit from the guarantees and facilities normally granted to the Staff Association in line with ESA Staff Regulations, Rules, and Instructions. b) participate to local health and safety committees in accordance with Section 4.7 of this policy. c) may assist staff members concerned by an incident or involved in internal legal proceedings relating to health and safety in line with the ESA applicable provisions. d) may alert or inform Administration of any issue detected or reported by staff m

Liaison between D epartments in charge of facilities management and personnel matters The Heads of the Departments in charge of facilities management and personnel matters will liaise to ensure consistent health and safety management within the Agency. This cooperation provides the background against which professional health and safety support is provided in the Agency. At site level, HSSEOs and HSE unit at ESTEC will liaise with the local Representative of the Department in charge of personnel matters to ensure that health and safety advice and assurance is complete and consistent. At site level, HSSEOs and HSE unit at ESTEC provide the health and safety assurance, co - ordination, promotion, and advisory functions set out in this policy. The ESTEC HSE unit contains safety, occupational health, and psychosocial risk expertise, and is headed by a professional health and sa fety advisor. 2. Contribution of HSSOs to corporate health and safety management. 2.1 Assistance to the Head of the Department in charge of facilities management HSSEOs and at ESTEC, the Head of the HSE unit will assist the Head of the Department in charge of facilities management to: a) prepare the annual report of health and safety for the executive board supporting the Director General. b) prepare the agenda and information needed by this board meeting. c) agree a programme of health and safety auditing. d) review an Agency framework for monitoring health and safety risk management. e) review criteria for: i) reporting safety incidents and occupational ill - health. ii) reporting healt h and safety risks. iii) site health and safety risk registers. E SA/ADMIN/IPOL - HESA ( 20 22) 1 P age 20 2.2 Preparation of annual health and safety report. Each HSSO and at ESTEC, the Head of the HSE Unit will prepare an annual health and safety report to the Heads of Establishments and Centres. Following endorsement by the Head of Establ

safety report. Each HSSO and at ESTEC, the Head of the HSE Unit will prepare an annual health and safety report to the Heads of Establishments and Centres. Following endorsement by the Head of Establishment or Centre concerned this report shall be forwarded to the Head of Department in charge of facilities management. The annual health and safety report will contain data as specified in the Agency framework for monitoring health and safety risk management. This data will: a) describe the incident and ill - health statistics o f the site. b) indicate the state of conformance of the site. c) detail the management of risks that meet corporate reporting criteria. 2.3. Health and safety management activities at sites. For the following health and safety management activities HSSEOs and the ESTEC HSE unit are to: a) assure by sampling, (e.g., physical inspections and audits) and incident investigations, that departments are adequately managing the health and safety risks arising from their activities. HSSEOs and H/HSE unit are to give special attention to risks that involve shared responsibilities across departments b) stop any activity that they believe creates inadequately managed health and safety risks to the people on site. The HSSEO and ESTEC H/HSE unit are accountable to the Head of Establishment for using this power c) monitor the state of conformity with the requirements of

lth and safety risks to the people on site. The HSSEO and ESTEC H/HSE unit are accountable to the Head of Establishment for using this power c) monitor the state of conformity with the requirements of health and safety legislation in the host country d) assure the readiness and effectiveness of site - wide emergency plans e) assure the readiness of the site to conform with changes in regulations or corporate requirements f) maintain and review register of on - site health and safety risks. ESTEC HSE unit is directly under the ESTEC Head of Establishment, while HSSEOs in respect of the above activities, report directl y to their Head of Establishment. The E SA/ADMIN/IPOL - HESA ( 20 22 )1 P age 21 specifics of what is to be reported and how, are to be formally agreed and documented between them. 2.4 Support to the site health and safety committee The HSSEO and the HSE unit at ESTEC, provides support to health and safety committees as directed by their Head of Establishment. The HSSEO and the HSE unit at ESTEC will report to their health and safety committee on the status of general health and safety risks (including occupational health and psycho - social risks) on sites. le on mission or tel eworking d) Technical Officers, about the health and safety requirements of contracts e) Technical Officers, about the management of health and safety risks arising from contract activities (including follow - up from HSSEO and the HSE unit at ESTEC monitoring act ivities) f) individuals who have been designated (by the Head of a Programme or Project) to act as a local expert on an aspect of risk health and safety management (e.g., laboratory safety). 2.6.2 In case of incidents In the event of any incident, the HSSEO and the HSE unit at ESTEC are to advise the Head of Department where the incident occurred, about the timeliness, technical competence, and lines of inquiry to be followed by the investigation 6 . The investigations are conducte d by the HSSEO and the HSE unit at ESTEC in collaboration with the relevant involved people. In case of major incidents the ESA/ADMIN/IPOL - RISK(2020)1 applies. The HSSEO and the HSE unit at ESTEC is to give advice as soon as possible, review the advice if new information arises and follow up in writing. In cases of occupational ill - health caused by the work environment, the HSSEO and the HSE unit at ESTEC will also liaise with the local head of HR. 2.6.3 Information about health and safety HSSEOs and the HSE unit at ESTEC are to ensure that the manpower resources and visitors to site, receive information about healt

se with the local head of HR. 2.6.3 Information about health and safety HSSEOs and the HSE unit at ESTEC are to ensure that the manpower resources and visitors to site, receive information about health and safety arrangements at the site (including emergency procedures). 3. (The safety management system includes all of the activities carried out by the Agency). E SA/ADMIN/IPOL - HESA ( 20 22 )1 P age 23 3.1.2 The Head of the Division in charge of facilities management manages the HSSEO function, is the line manager of the HSSEO, and provides the interface between the HSSEO and the Agency as an employer when the HSSEO is a member of Staff. The HSSEO reports directly to the Head of Establishment in case of hea lth and safety issues. The Head of the HSE unit at ESTEC reports directly to the ESTEC Head of Establishment 3.1.3 Where the HSSO is a contractor; the Head of the Division in charge of facilities management will be the technical representative of the Agen cy to be designated under the contract through which the HSSO services are procured. 3.2 HSSOs and the HSE unit

pecialisations required as part of the HSSEO’s and the HSE unit at ESTEC employment). 4. Resources must be kept under constant review by the Agency. ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public Introduction of ESA Cooperative Agreements to Industry ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public Page 2 / 6 Introduction of ESA Cooperative Agreements to Industry 1. Introduction As part of the Agency’s mandate to support Space industry competitiveness, the Ministerial Council Resolution on “ESA Accelerating the Use of Space in Europe” calls upon ESA to “ develop forward - looking tools for accompanying and stimulating the commercialisation of space activities through innovative support to European commercial actors ”. Therefore, to unlock new commercial potential , partnership models and procurement methods, is integrat ed in the Regulations , in the form of the contracting method of Calls for Proposals without Procurement with the use of Cooperative Agreement as a legal instrument for the implementation of partnership with Industry. In these activities, ESA funds eligible activities to be carried out by the Partner. ESA also provides technical support and validation of the activities, without being the end customer of resulting goods or services in the concrete tender action. In essence, Calls for Proposals without Procurement, and the resulting Cooperative Agreements, laid down in the new Article 10 of the Regulations , is remarkably similar to the Calls and contracts put in place up to now for the implementation of Close - to -

e resulting Cooperative Agreements, laid down in the new Article 10 of the Regulations , is remarkably similar to the Calls and contracts put in place up to now for the implementation of Close - to - Market or support to innovation Programmes such as ARTES C&G, ARTES Partnership, BASS, Scale - up Invest, Incubed, NAVISP Element 2, Boost 1! , etc. This in particular provides for a preliminary stage, eligibility conditions, and co - funding requirements. With this in mind, the provisions of the Cooperative Agreement will be largely similar to those foreseen under procurement contracts. However, since there is no acquisition of goods or services, there are essentially two key advantages rendering a Cooperative Agreement better suited to implement these activities than a procurement contract: a. General provisions are adapted to a situation which involves partnership on equilibrated terms, technical support, and co - funding by the Agency, rather than procurement of goods, technology or services by a customer from a supplier, with clauses on accepta nce, warranty, penalties , etc., which is not the real situation in a partnership. This feature alone makes a Cooperative A greement more suitable for a partnership than a classic procurement contract. b. In particular, the intellectual property regime should reflect the situation of a partnership where ESA supports the development of p

suitable for a partnership than a classic procurement contract. b. In particular, the intellectual property regime should reflect the situation of a partnership where ESA supports the development of products and services for private and public customers, rather than a situation where ESA procures a system or services. The definitions and other terms of the intellectual property regime need to be readily understood by external stakeholders , e.g. venture capitalists and new entrants to the relatively niche space industry. Since the Agency is not taking delivery in a product or system, there is no need for ESA to claim extensive access to background rights in know - how and trade secrets. The Calls for Proposals without Procurement is a tool to help Industry develop key technologies and products that can enable new services to be offered later to commercial or public customers. Future programmes may contain the possibility to introduce Calls for P roposals without Procurement as well as public procurement of hardware or services, as separate individual tender actions. at the same time supporting the competitiveness of European industry (i.e. IPR ownership vested with contractors). Compared to the current tailoring of the GCC Part II as reflected in the draft co - funded contract ( A rticle 5, Part II) with either Option A or B depending on the co - funding level, the following main modifications are foreseen in the IPR regime of the Cooperative A greement: - The definition of IPR does not include know - how and trade secrets; - The access rights, or the licence to use, is limited to Registered IPR for both ESA and Participating States only when required for “space research and technology and their space applications ”. The access rights in Registered IPR secures the possibility for ESA and its Participating States to use Registered IPR for its core activities in return for the provided co - funding. On the other hand, for downstream activities and non - space applications, IPR access will NOT be necessary for ESA and Participating States. This is an important change to reassure investors and industrial partners in support of the credibility of the partner business plans and competitiveness of European economic operators. Overall, ESA is confident that the tailoring of the IPR regime answers to concerns expressed by Industry on the balance of rights and obligations with respect to IPR, in particular for partnerships.

CLAUSE 2 - APPROBATION En matière de contrats, les offres et les acceptations n'engageront l'Agence que lorsqu'elles auront reçu l'approbation écrite du Directeur Général ou de son représentant autorisé. Sauf disposition contraire du contrat, la date de ladite approbation constituera la date de commencement du contrat. CLAUSE 3 - LANGUES UTILISEES Le contrat ainsi que les documents joints seront normalement établis en anglais ou en français au choix du contractant, à moins que des circonstances spéciales ne requièrent l'emploi d'une autre langue. Ces exemplaires originaux sont destinés aux parties contractantes. ESA/C/290, rév 6 page 61 ANNEXE I aux CONDITIONS GENERALES RELATIVES AUX CONTRATS DE L'ASE PREMIERE PARTIE - DETERMINATION DES PRIX CLAUSE 1 - TYPES DE PRIX 1.1 Lorsqu'un des types de prix énumérés à la clause 1.2 est m entionné dans le contrat, il s'entend au sens donné à la clause correspondante de la première Partie de la présente annexe et est régi par les dispositions qui y sont énoncées. 1.2 Les types de prix visés à la clause 1.1 sont les suivants: a) Prix forfaitaire: - prix forfaitaire définitif - prix forfaitaire comportant une clause de variation - prix unitaire forfaitaire b) Prix plafond à convertir en prix forfaitaire c) Prix calculé sur base de remboursement des frais: - en dépenses contrôlées plus rémunérations forfaitaires - en dépenses contrôlées plus intéressement - en heures contrôlées. CLAUSE 5 - DISPOSITIONS APPLICA BLES AUX CONTRATS A PRIX CALCULE SUR LA BASE DE REMBOURSEMENT DE FRAIS Les dispositions des clauses 6, 7 et 8 de la présente annexe s'appliquent a tous les contrats conclus sur la base d'un remboursement des frais, ainsi que dans le cas prévu à la clau se 3.4. Le contractant devra faire figurer les mêmes conditions que celles y mentionnées dans tous les sous - contrats à prix calculé sur la base de remboursement de frais avec un sous - traitant. CLAUSE 7 - CATEGORIES DES DEPENSES 7.1 Pour l'évaluation ou le calcul des coûts des fournitures à livrer ou des services à prester en exécution du contrat, le contractant doit distinguer les catégories des dépenses suivantes: a) Frais

7.1 Pour l'évaluation ou le calcul des coûts des fournitures à livrer ou des services à prester en exécution du contrat, le contractant doit distinguer les catégories des dépenses suivantes: a) Frais directs Les frais directs sont ceux que l'on peut imputer spécifiquement au contrat. Les frais directs ne sont pas limités à des éléments incorporés dans le produit final tels que matériaux ou main - d'oeuvre. b) Frai s indirects Les frais indirects sont ceux qui n'ont pas été classés dans la catégorie des frais directs. 7.2 Le contractant donnera la répartition des frais entre les deux catégories: frais directs et frais indirects. La méthode suivant laquelle les frais sont classés comme frais directs ou indirects ne peut subir aucune modification pendant la durée du contrat. CLAUSE 8 - TAUX DE FRAIS GENERAUX 8.1 Les frais indirects qui doivent, en règle générale, être imputés à l'ensemble des travaux du contract ant, seront classés par catégories suivant une ventilation logique, conforme aux principes comptables rationnels et aux pratiques habituelles du contractant, et présentes sous forme de taux, dits: "taux de frais généraux", applicables aux diverses catégori es de frais directs auxquelles ils se rapportent. 8.2 Le contractant est tenu d'informer l'Agence de ses taux de frais généraux et de la base sur lesquels ils s'appliquent. Par "taux provisoires de frais généraux", on e

auxquelles ils se rapportent. 8.2 Le contractant est tenu d'informer l'Agence de ses taux de frais généraux et de la base sur lesquels ils s'appliquent. Par "taux provisoires de frais généraux", on entend le pourcentage de frais géné raux convenu à titre temporaire aux fins de facturation en attendant la fixation du taux définitif de frais généraux. Un taux de frais généraux est définitif lorsqu'il a été accepté comme tel d'un commun accord par l'Agence et par le contractant. 8.3 Un taux de frais généraux est fixé "a priori" s'il est fixé avant ou pendant une certaine période et basé sur les frais (évalués) à engager au cours de cette période. Un taux de frais généraux est déterminé "a posteriori" s'il est fixé après une certaine pé riode et base sur des frais effectivement engagés au cours de cette période. ESA/C/290, rév. 6 page 70 a) Les taux de frais généraux "fixés a priori" doivent, d'un commun accord, être établis autant que possible avant le début de la période durant laquelle ils seront appliqués. En cas d'impossibilité, le contrat stipulera, en nombre de jours, le délai dans lequel l'accord sur les taux devra intervenir. Dans ce cas, le contrat indiquera également les limites inférieures et supérieures entre lesquelles les taux devront être fixés. Si l'accord n'est pas réalise à la fin du délai prescrit et / ou dans les limites convenues, les taux de frais généraux s

mites inférieures et supérieures entre lesquelles les taux devront être fixés. Si l'accord n'est pas réalise à la fin du délai prescrit et / ou dans les limites convenues, les taux de frais généraux seront déterminés a posteriori. Les taux de frais généraux déterminés à l'avance sont fixés soit pour la durée totale de l'exécutio n du contrat, soit pour une période plus courte, fixée d'un commun accord. b) Les taux de frais généraux déterminés "a posteriori" sont fixés le plus tot possible après la fin de chaque exercice financier annuel du contractant. Le contractant doit, le p lus tôt possible après la fin de chaque exercice, proposer à l'Agence des taux définitifs de frais généraux pour cette période, en se fondant sur les dépenses qu'il a effectivement supportées, et fournir toutes pièces justificatives à l'appui. 8.4 Les rés ultats des négociations font chaque fois l'objet d'un avenant au contrat ou sont précisés: - les taux finaux agréés - les bases sur lesquelles les taux s'appliquent, et - les périodes pour lesquelles les taux s'appliquent. CLAUSE 9 - LIMITATION D'ENGA GEMENT 9.1 La limitation d'engagement est un montant spécifié dans le contrat et correspondant au maximum des paiements que l'Agence s'engage à effectuer et qui ne peut être augmenté que par accord écrit de l'Agence. 9.2 Si, à un moment quelconque, le co ntractant a des raisons de penser que les frais qu'i

es paiements que l'Agence s'engage à effectuer et qui ne peut être augmenté que par accord écrit de l'Agence. 9.2 Si, à un moment quelconque, le co ntractant a des raisons de penser que les frais qu'il devra supporter pour l'exécution du contrat au cours des soixante (60) jours suivants, ajoutés à tous les frais déjà encourus, dépasseront soixante - quinze pour cent (75%) du montant de la limitation d'e ngagement, le contractant en informera l'Agence par écrit en soumettant l'estimation révisée du coût total. 9.3 L'Agence ne sera pas tenue de rembourser au contractant les frais engagés en sus de la limitation d'engagement, et le contractant n'est pas ten u de poursuivre l'exécution du marché, ni de supporter des frais supérieurs au montant de la limitation d'engagement prévue, si et tant que l'Agence ne lui a pas notifié par écrit que la limitation a été révisée et portée à un montant supérieur. Tous les frais engagés par le contractant en sus de cette limitation, avant l'approbation de l'augmentation sont considérés comme admissibles dans la mesure où ils seraient considérés comme tels s'ils avaient été engagés après cette augmentation. Vorkalkulatorische Gemeinkostensätze werd en entweder für die gesamte Dauer des Vertrages oder einen kürzeren, in beiderseitigem Einvernehmen festzulegenden Zeitraum vereinbart. b) Nachkalkulatorische Gemeinkostensätze werden jeweils so früh wie möglich nach Ablauf des Geschäftsjahres des Auftragnehm ers vereinbart. Der Auftragnehmer muß der Organisati

en Zeitraum vereinbart. b) Nachkalkulatorische Gemeinkostensätze werden jeweils so früh wie möglich nach Ablauf des Geschäftsjahres des Auftragnehm ers vereinbart. Der Auftragnehmer muß der Organisation so rasch wie möglich nach Ablauf des Geschäftsjahres unter Zugrundelegung der ihm tatsächlich entstandenen Kosten, für die Belege beizubringen sind, endgültige Gemeinkostensätze für das betreffende Jahr vorschlagen. 8.4 Die Verhandlungsergebnisse werden jeweils in einem Zusatzvertrag mit folgenden Angaben niedergelegt: − die vereinbarten endgültigen Sätze, − die Zuschlagsbasen, auf die diese Sätze angewandt werden, − die Zeiträume, für die diese Sätze gelten. ARTIKEL 11 ENTWICKLUNGSKOSTENPLAN 11.1 Der Auftragnehmer legt einen Entwicklungskoste nplan vor; dieser ist eine ausführliche mit Zahlenangaben versehene Planungsunterlage für die bis zur Vollendung des Projektes durchzuführenden technischen Arbeiten; die Ar beiten sind in Abschnitte eingeteilt, für die Abwicklungszeiträume und der Kostenaufwand ve ranschlagt sind, so daß während der Dauer des Projektes der bis zu einem gegebenen Zeitpunkt erzielte Programmfortschritt und die bis dahin angefallenen Kosten mit den ursprünglichen Schätzungen verglichen werden können. 11.2 Falls im Vertrag vorgesehen, wird der Entwicklungskostenplan dem Vertrag als Anlage beigefügt. 11.3 Im Entwicklungskostenplan sind, nach Vierteljahren aufgeschlüsselt, die voraussichtlichen Gesamtkosten der im Entwicklungsplan aufgef ührten technischen Positionen anzugeben. Die Kostenschätzung muß auf das technische Pr ogramm bezogen sein, und der Auftragnehmer darf auf keinen Fall einen Zuschlag für unvor hergesehene allgemeine Mehrkosten einsetzen. Die Kostenansätze für die verschiedenen technischen Positionen müssen jedoch auch die Arbeiten einschließen, die sich nur ungenau a bgrenzen oder kalkulieren lassen. Sie müssen auch auf Erfahrung beruhende Zuschläge fü r Verzögerungen und Schwierigkeiten enthalten, die bei derartigen Pro

beiten einschließen, die sich nur ungenau a bgrenzen oder kalkulieren lassen. Sie müssen auch auf Erfahrung beruhende Zuschläge fü r Verzögerungen und Schwierigkeiten enthalten, die bei derartigen Programmen bekanntlich auftreten können, soweit sie die Entwicklungsarbeiten beeinträchtigen. ESA/C/290, rev.6 Seite 76 b) Lieferung von Seriengerät: für jeden Tag Verzug bei der Lieferung des Seriengeräts: 0,4 vom Tausend vom ersten bis einschließlich vierzigsten Tag; 1 vom Tausend für jeden weiteren Tag bis höchstens 10 % der im Vertrag nach Artikel 28 festgelegten Gesamtschätzung. c) Werden der Prototyp und das Seriengerät im Rahmen desselben Vertrages geliefert, so gilt der nach Buchstabe b anwendbare Sa tz von 0,4 vom Tausend pro Tag während vierzig Tagen abzüglich der Zahl der Tage, fü r die eine Vertragsstrafe wegen verspäteter Lieferung des Prototyps verhängt wurde. 2.2 Selbstkostenerstattungsvertrag mit Anreizgewinn: Die Vertragsstrafen bestimmen sich nach Artikel 4 Absatz 2 der Anlage I. 3. Principes d’application de la nouvelle Clause 46 des Clauses et conditions générales relatives aux contrats de l’ASE 1. Introduction Dans la version 5 précédente des Clauses et conditions générales relatives aux contrats de l’ASE (CCG), le terme « redev ance » (royalty) faisait référence à la rémunération versée dans certains cas à l’Agence par un contractant exploitant les droits de propriété intellectuelle de celle - ci. Le terme « royalty » est communément utilisé pour signifier la rémunération périodiqu e versée au titulaire d’un brevet par une personne autorisée à l’exploiter. C’est la raison pour laquelle, dans la version 6 des CCG, on a préféré utiliser en anglais l’expression plus neutre de « fee » (traduite en français par « reversement financier ») pour évoquer la rémunération versée à l’Agence dans des cas spécifiques. La Clause 46 des CCG n’indique que les principes de base et les restrictions générales, sans entrer dans le détail des critères de fixation et de paiement des montants à reverser. O n trouvera ci - après les directives concernant l’application de la Clause 46. 2. Détermination du taux des reversements (a) Application selon le type d’accord De manière générale, aucun reversement ne doit être exigé sur la vente d’un produit. La vente d ’un produit en dehors des États membres ne doit donner lieu à reversement que dans des cas exceptionnels et lorsque les

ale, aucun reversement ne doit être exigé sur la vente d’un produit. La vente d ’un produit en dehors des États membres ne doit donner lieu à reversement que dans des cas exceptionnels et lorsque les États participant au programme de l’Agence concerné le décident expressément. En conséquence, des reversements ne doivent en règle génér ale être envisagés que dans le cas d’un accord de licence. Dans ce cas, deux restrictions sont prises en considération : • En règle générale, des reversements ne doivent être prévus que pour les licences autorisant la production d’articles développés au tit re d’un contrat de l’ASE. C’est le cas, par exemple, d’une licence autorisant l’accès non limité au code source d’un programme informatique, ce qui permet de modifier le logiciel pour créer différentes applications. • Les contractants doivent également pouv oir exploiter les résultats d’un projet sur le territoire des États membres à des conditions favorables. Par conséquent, des reversements ne sont exigés que dans le cadre de licences délivrées à une personne établie dans des États non membres. (b) Méthode s de calcul et seuil Le montant des reversements est calculé en fonction des recettes effectives (c’est - à - dire des recettes provenant de l’exploitation des licences, déduction faite de tout impôt payé par le contractant sur celles - ci) car cette méthode pe rmet de placer tous les contr

tives (c’est - à - dire des recettes provenant de l’exploitation des licences, déduction faite de tout impôt payé par le contractant sur celles - ci) car cette méthode pe rmet de placer tous les contractants sur un pied d’égalité. Les reversements ne sont exigibles qu’à partir du moment où l’exploitation des résultats du projet devient exceptionnellement rentable. Les recettes doivent par conséquent dépasser le seuil de 5 00 keuros avant l’établissement d’un système de reversement. Dans le régime de l’ASE, ce seuil s’appliquera de manière générale aux recettes provenant des licences. Ce n’est que dans les cas exceptionnels où les États membres décideront d’imposer un revers ement sur les ventes réalisées en dehors de leur territoire que le seuil s’appliquera aussi aux ventes. Le seuil sera déclenché dès lors que les recettes cumulées provenant de l’exploitation des licences de production d’articles dépasseront 500 keuros. Le reversement sera appliqué sur le total des recettes cumulées. (c) Taux Dans le cas d’une licence de production d’articles, l’ASE demandera au contractant de lui reverser un certain pourcentage des droits qu’il a lui - même perçus au titre de la licence. De ux cas de figure sont envisagés : • Pour les licences dans le domaine des applications spatiales et non spatiales dont le bénéficiaire est établi en dehors des États membres, il est appliqué un taux unifo

as de figure sont envisagés : • Pour les licences dans le domaine des applications spatiales et non spatiales dont le bénéficiaire est établi en dehors des États membres, il est appliqué un taux uniforme compris entre 5 et 10 % des redevances perçues pa r le contractant. L’instauration d’un ensemble de conditions uniformes s’impose dans la mesure où aucun facteur de différentiation ne justifie de traiter différemment les applications spatiales et non spatiales. • En cas de transfert de technologie 1 en deho rs des États membres, un taux légèrement supérieur sera demandé. Dans la mesure où l’Agence a investi dans le transfert du produit vers le secteur non spatial, l’application d’un taux compris entre 10 et 20 % des redevances perçues par le contractant se ju stifie. Le taux exact du reversement sera arrêté d’un commun accord avec le ou les soumissionnaires et figurera dans le contrat correspondant. (d) Limite supérieure et restrictions Le montant total des reversements dus à l’Agence ne peut excéder le to tal des frais engagés par celle - ci pour la fourniture des travaux ou des droits exploités. L’obligation de reversement cesse dix ans après la date de réception par l’Agence des travaux correspondants. Aucun reversement n’est dû pour des licences concédées à titre gratuit quand la situation est conforme aux clauses 41 et 42 (par exemple dans le cas d’une licence accordée à u

travaux correspondants. Aucun reversement n’est dû pour des licences concédées à titre gratuit quand la situation est conforme aux clauses 41 et 42 (par exemple dans le cas d’une licence accordée à un tiers pour des droits de propriété intellectuelle découlant de travaux réalisés dans le cadre du contrat pour les besoins propres à ca ractère public de l’Agence). (e) Exceptions ou adaptations dans le cas de certains programmes Les États participants peuvent adopter des règles spécifiques en ce qui concerne les reversements pour tenir compte des objectifs particuliers de ces programm es. Le règlement d’exécution d’un programme peut ainsi préciser le montant à reverser en cas d’exploitation par le contractant des résultats dudit programme ou décider d’une exemption pour en respecter les objectifs particuliers. 1 Un programme de transfert de technologie est une activité dans laquelle l’ASE investit afin qu’un produit ayant une application spatiale puisse faire l’objet d’une application terrestre. BACKGROUND In ESA’s Tender Actions and more in general in procurements made within ESA Programmes, any price quotation, irrespective of the price type, must be justified by bidders and detailed by using standard Price Breakdown Forms (previously PSS - A forms), in shor t ‘PBF’. The PBF are price reports produced with the ECOS software. The use of ECOS is mandatory for large projects (i.e. ESA Tender Actions with an overall price above EUR 10M across all contractual phases). For Tender Actions of lower value, the use of ECOS is an optional choice, unless differently indicated in the specific Conditions to Tender or price requirements. Even when the use of ECOS is not mandatory, the ESA Industrial Audit Office and the ESA Cost Engineering Section highly recommend the use of ECOS for the preparation of a compliant price proposal. In all cases where the bidder decides not to use ECOS, the price breakdown presentation shall respect the format of the PBF. For this reason, a template of the PBF is available as MS Excel file and published in esa - star. Tailoring or modification of the PB F is not allowed and may result in the down - marking or the rejection of the offer. Bidders bear the responsibility to ensure a correct calculation of the price. Where ECOS is not mandatory, the Tender Action Data Package shall inc

Where ECOS is not mandatory, the Tender Action Data Package shall include the required details to be presented in PBF. Typically, the requirement of: • PBF1 (PSS - A2) is always mandatory; Annexes to PBF1 may be decided by the TEB. • PBF2 (PSS - A8) may be decided by the TEB. • PBF3 (PSS - A10 and 15) may be decided by the TEB. Any other pre - defined price reports or PBF can only be printed using ECOS. 2. PBF LOGIC The three main PBF (i.e. PBF - 1, PBF - 2, PBF - 3), including all annexes, provide ESA with full visibility of the quoted price: • PBF - 1 shows the total price, broken down by price elements. The annexes provide cost details which appear consolidated in the main PBF tables. The standard price elements in ESA contracts are the following: • Labour cost • Internal Special Facilities cost • Other Direct Costs (Materials, External Services, Miscellaneous, Travel) • Profit fee • Cost Without Additional Charges • Company Contributions These elements are retained in

PRICE CONDITIONS The price conditions are normally part of the costing requirements published by ESA, or by the issuing entity in cases on non - ESA Tender Actions. Price type and economic conditions The price type refers to the definitions included in the ESA/REG/002 Annex II. In case of Firm and Fixed Price (FFP) and Ceiling Price to be converted to Firm and Fixed Price (CP - >FFP), the price shall cover the inflation of prices over the planned full duration of the contract. The term ‘Firm’ means that no adjustment for price inflation can be done after the signature of the contract. The term ‘Fixed’ means that no adjustmen t of the price can be done as result of the actual cost incurred. In case of Fixed Price with price Variation (FPV) the cost shall respect the required economic conditions (i.e. the overall state of economy in the Country of the bidder at a given year and month; e.g. 07/2025) and therefore the financial inflation shall not be included. This type of price represents a risk sharing scheme on financial inflation: a formula bas ed on inflation indices is agreed in advance and used to compensate the general inflation of prices. Currency Bidders are required to calculate the price using the National Currency (NC) of their Country of registration (unless the entity accounts are recorded using a different currency). The price of ESA contracts is normally agreed in the EURO currency, bidders in Countries non adopting the EURO must propose a currency exchange rate. • For FFP, the exchange rate used should be one representative of the period for which the work will be performed. When proposing a reasonable exchange rate, companies should refer to the European Central Bank publications. An analysis based on the duration of the contract may consider an average rate based on spot rates published in the past 6 - months or 1 - year and considering trends for extrapolation of possible future evolutions. A reasonable margin based on the volatility of the rate may be consi

A reasonable margin based on the volatility of the rate may be considered acceptable to protect the contractor financial exposure and to limit cost of hedging. • For FPV, the exchange rate used must be the one published on the ESA Price Statistics Bulletin for the month and year of the required economic conditions. The reason for this requirement is linked to the use of EURO indices in the Price Variation Formula; these special indices produced for ESA include the effect of the exchange rate variation and assume the values published (which refer to the European Central Bank). 4. LABOUR COST Labour cost refers to the cost of direct personnel to execute the contractual tasks. The PBF require s that direct personnel is grouped by ‘labour categories’ or cost centres, and that an average cost rate for each category of labour is charged to the number of hours quoted to perform the work. The cost rate shall be comprehensive of direct costs (i.e. salaries and social charges), as well as any direct (e.g. other personnel costs) and indirect (e.g. General & Administration) overheads; this combination is referred to as ‘gross rate’. The allowable cost is described within the Annex I of the ESA/REG/002. ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public ESA UNCLASSIFI

ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public Page 6 / 15 The bidder shall quote • the number of hours necessary to perform the work; • the gross labour hourly rates; • the average productive hours of each labour category. Productive hours Bidders shall refer to the ESA definition of productive hours : the normal number of hours that direct personnel record to funded and partially funded activities, including any self - funded R&D. The word ‘normal’ refers to the requirement that the rates and overheads allocated to each unit of production shall not be significantly influenced as a consequence of a particular economic situation, abnormal production, uncommon practices or idle facilit ies/personnel. In essence, for the calculation of the productive hours, the bidder shall consider an optimal production level. The following tasks are excluded from productive hours : Proposals and Tenders, Training, internal general meetings, administrative, management and other non - productive time. It is expected in general that the average productive hours are within 75 - 95% of the average worked hours. Worked hours are related to the personnel work conditions and exclude any sort of absence. The bidders shall define the cost to be charged via the ISF rates, which may include the depreciation of the acquisition cost, maintenance, set - up and even operations, including the cost of dedicated operators where relevant. Possibly a portion of the comp any G&A expenditures may be added to the charged cost rates. The unit of charge depends on the operation of each ISF. For example, a Clean Room may be charged by sqm/day; a manufacturing workstation by operations hours. The cost allocated to ISF rates shall be excluded from the company overheads charged on Labour or procurements. Audited and non - audited entities The ISF rates quoted by audited and non - audited entities shall respect the same requirements as for Labour rates. 6. The maximum percentage is normally calculated in accordance with the applicable ESA Profit Policy. In some type of contracts, e.g. co - funded, the profit fee may be considered not allowable . Cost Without Additional Charge Cost Without Additional Charge (CWAC) are expenses incurred on behalf of the customer and necessary for the execution of the project that are directly charged back to the customer without a markup, functioning as a reimbursement. These third - party costs, such as special support equipment , IPR license fees , services from third - parties or regulatory fees, pass through the vendor's books but are not meant to attract overheads nor generate profit. Annex E provides a s t andard tabl e to report some details of the quoted CWAC. In particular, the bidder can indicate whether the CWAC is a Pass - Through cost or a special Fee . This type of costs includes the value of Customer Furnished Items (CFI) which will not be added to the total price, but it will form part of the total value of the goods delivered. SUBCONTRACTORS A sub - contract is a contract to be entered into by the bidder with a third party for a clearly defined task, related and necessary to the proposed scope of work, and which is sufficiently non - standard to require specifications/deliverables to be procured w ith a relevant third - party. It is thus distinguished from a Purchase Order, which is placed on the basis of standard documents or a price list from commercial suppliers. Subcontractors must be responsible for one or more work - packages of the WBS presented to ESA. The cost of a Subcontractor is NOT reported within the Company Costs, neither as an ODC nor as a CWAC. A bidder is not allowed to charge any overhead nor profit on its subcontractors cost. Subcontractors are responsible to produce their own set of PBF. SÉCURITÉ Les Parties adoptent des mesures de sécurité techniques et organisationnelles appropriées, en tenant dûment compte des risques inhérents au Traitement ainsi que de la nature, du champ d’application, du contexte et de l’objet de ce Traitement, afin d’assurer, le cas échéant : la confidentialité, l’intégrité, la disponibilité et la résilience continues des systèmes et services de Traitement ; la protection des Données personnelles contre tout accès, utilisation, destruction, perte, modification ou transfert accidentel, illégal ou non autorisé. 8. ADMINISTRATEUR CHARGÉ DE LA PROTECTION DES DONNÉES/PERSONNE À CONTACTER Pour toute question relative à la protection des Données personnelles, les Parties se réfèrent à leurs personnes à contacter, désignées à cet effet dans le Contrat. 9. TRANSFERT La Partie ayant reçu des Données personnelles de l’autre Partie au titre du Contrat ne traite (et ne fait traiter par ses sous-traitants autorisés ou agents autorisés chargés, dans le cadre de contrats de sous-traitance, du traitement des données) ces Données personnelles que sur le Territoire approuvé de traitement. Dans le cas où les Parties conviendraient du contraire, le transfert des Données personnelles hors du Territoire approuvé sera effectué conformément à l’article 13 infra. 10. ATTEINTE AUX DONNÉES PERSONNELLES 11.1 Une Partie qui constate une atteinte aux Données personnelles relevant de sa responsabilité et affectant des Données personnelles communiquées par l’autre Partie, dispose de 48 heures pour en informer cette dernière. 11.2 Les Parties se fournissent l’une à l’autre une assistance raisonnable afin de faciliter la prise en charge de cette atteinte aux Données personnelles ainsi que des informations précises sur cette dernière, en particulier si elle donne ou est susceptible de donner lieu au dépôt d’une plainte par une Personne concernée. 12. LÉGISLATION – RÈGLEMENT DES DIFFÉRENDS En matière de protection des Données personnelles, nonobstant toute autre disposition de la législation applicable énoncée ailleurs dans le Contrat, les dispositions figurant dans la Réglementation relative à la confidentialité des données visée dans le présent document s’appliquent comme indiqué au point 2 supra et prévalent en cas de conflit. PART 1 - CONDITIONS FOR PARTICIPATING IN A TENDER ACTION Eligibility Requirements The below eligibility requirements to participate in a Tender Action of the Agency are stemming from Article 12 of the Contracting Regulations. Registration Requirements The ESA Member States have made registration mandatory for Economic Operators wishing to do business with the Agency as stipulated in Article 12.5 of the Contracting Regulations. Economic Operators not yet registered as potential Bidders are requested to complete the online questionnaire on the “esa-star Registration” website (https://esastar-emr.sso.esa.int/). ESA UNCLASSIFIED – Releasable to the Public ESA/ C (2022) 104 Annex 1 Page 1 ANNEX I ESA PROFIT POLICY 1. Purpose The purpose of this document is to provide a policy for the profit determination in procurements of the European Space Agency (ESA). This is achieved by establishing a standard methodology for the determination of a fair and reasonable profit linked to risk, providing transparency and understanding to all stakehol ders and allowing to: – Reward contractors fairly and reasonably commensurate with risk; – Treat all contractors equitably and in a consistent manner; – Incentivise and sustain the European space industry in a competitive environment and; – Achieve value for mone y in ESA procurements. This profit policy is meant to define a reference baseline regarding profit determination at any level of the supply chain, whenever the procurement could be considered in the frame of the Space procurement. The Executive is expected to use this policy in implementing its programmes, bearing in mind that modalities can be adapted to better fit the particularities of each individual project and/or procurement action. The implementation modalities of this profit policy (i.e. Pro fit fee and minimum level of Management Reserve) will be outlined in the relevant procurement proposal to the IPC, bearing in mind that further refinement can be made in the ITT as a result of the Pre

This profit policy is not applicable to General procurement. The Profit Policy is a combination of (1) an adequate Profit Rate commensurate to the risks taken and (2) a further improvement of Contractual Risk Sharing provisions. 2. Pro fit Rate The procurements of ESA allow for the contractors to apply a ‘Profit Rate’, defined as a margin between the contractual price and the declared cost. This rate is calculated on the basis of the relevant eligible costs (as defined in the Annex 1 to the GCC - ESA REG/002 rev.3) of each company. When determining the allowable Profit Rate there needs to be a clear understanding of the types of risks endorsed in the various types of contracts and activities. The greater the risk accepted by the contractor the greater the profit allowance should be. Such requirements are approved by the Agency’s Industrial Policy Committee (IPC) in accordance with Article 17 of the Agency’s Procurement Regulations (ESA/REG/001) at its latest revision . Evaluation Criteria Evaluation criteria are the norms to be applied by the TEB to determine the strengths and weaknesses of a tender by separate evaluations of its various aspects. The identification of specific significant evaluation criteria is more essential than the identification of a multitude of criteria c overing all possible minor aspects. Evaluation criteria shall be well defined and logically distinct. They shall cover all aspects of a tender and shall avoid duplication. The criteria shall be divided into technical criteria, such as understanding of and compliance with requirements, quality and suitability of proposed design, and suitability of facilities and of support programme, and management criteria, such as overall organisation and management methods, costing and planning, manpower deployment, e xperience and capacity of the tenderer, and compliance with substantive tender a

Price shall not be a criteria. (See, however, section 7.4.2.7 on the overall assessment of tenders, including the price). On 31 December 1975, the Convention was signed by Ireland . The Convention entered into force on 30 October 1980 . 7 In accordance with Article XVI, 3 of the Convention, the Council has amended certain provisions in Annexes to the Convention adopting the following: • ESA/C-M/CXXII/Res . 1 (Final), chapter IV, adopted on 20 October 1995; • ESA/C-M/CLIV/Res . 2 (Final), chapter III, adopted on 15 November 2001; • ESA/C/CLXXIX/Res . 6 (Final), adopted on 22 June 2005; • ESA/C(2009)73, adopted on 10 June 2009 . 7 Italy: 20 February 1978 United Kingdom: 28 March 1978 Belgium: 3 October 1978 Netherlands: 6 February 1979 Spain: 7 February 1979 France: 30 October 1980 Ireland: 10 December 1980 Austria: 30 December 1986 Norway: 30 December 1986 Finland: 1 January 1995 Portugal: 14 November 2000 Greece: 9 March 2005 Luxembourg: 30 June 2005 Czech Republic: 12 November 2008 Romania: 22 December 2011 Poland: 19 November 2012 Estonia: 1 September 2015 Hungary: 4 November 2015 Slovenia: 1 January 2025 9 10 CONVENTION FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A EUROPEAN SPACE AGENCY The States parties to this Convention, CONSIDERING that the magnitude of the human, technical and financial resources required for activities in the space field is such that these resources lie beyond the means of any single European country, CONSIDERING the Resolution adopted by the European Space Conference on 20 December 1972 and confirmed by the European Space Conference on 31 July 1973, which decided that a new organisation, called the ‘European Space Agency’, would be formed out of the European Space Research Organisation and the European Organisation for the Development and Construction of Space Vehicle Launchers, and that the aim would be to integrate the European national space programmes into a European space programme as far and as fast as reasonably possible, DESIRING to pursue and to strengthen European cooperation, for

would be to integrate the European national space programmes into a European space programme as far and as fast as reasonably possible, DESIRING to pursue and to strengthen European cooperation, for exclusively peaceful purposes, in space research and technology and their space applications, with a view to their being used 11 for scientific purposes and for operational space applications systems, DESIRING, in order to achieve these aims, to establish a single European space organisation to increase the efficiency of the total of European space efforts by making better use of the resources at present devoted to space and to define a European space programme for exclusively peaceful purposes, HAVE AGREED as follows: Article I ESTABLISHMENT OF THE AGENCY 1. A European organisation, called the ‘European Space Agency’, hereinafter referred to as ‘the Agency’, is hereby established. 2. The members of the Agency, hereinafter referred to as ‘Member States’, shall be the States which are parties to this Convention in accordance with Articles XX and XXII. 3. All Member States shall participate in the mandatory activities referred to in Article V, 1 a , and shall contribute to the fixed common costs of the Agency, referred to in Annex II. 12 4. The Headquarters of the Agency shall be situated in the Paris area. Article II PURPOSE The purpose of the Agency shall be to provide for and to p

on costs of the Agency, referred to in Annex II. 12 4. The Headquarters of the Agency shall be situated in the Paris area. Article II PURPOSE The purpose of the Agency shall be to provide for and to promote, for exclusively peaceful purposes, cooperation among European States in space research and technology and their space applications, with a view to their being used for scientific purposes and for operational space applications systems: a . by elaborating and implementing a long-term European space policy, by recommending space objectives to the Member States, and by concerting the policies of the Member States with respect to other national and international organisations and institutions; b . by elaborating and implementing activities and programmes in the space field; c . by coordinating the European space programme and national programmes, and by integrating the latter progressively and as completely as possible into the European space programme, 13 in particular as regards the development of applications satellites; d . by elaborating and implementing the industrial policy appropriate to its programme and by recommending a coherent industrial policy to the Member States. Article III INFORMATION AND DATA 1. Member States and the Agency shall facilitate the exchange of scientific and technical information pertaining to the fields of space research and technology and their

ticle III INFORMATION AND DATA 1. Member States and the Agency shall facilitate the exchange of scientific and technical information pertaining to the fields of space research and technology and their space applications, provided that a Member State shall not be required to communicate any information obtained outside the Agency if it considers that such communication would be inconsistent with the interests of its own security or its own agreements with third parties, or the conditions under which such information has been obtained. 2. In carrying out its activities under Article V, the Agency shall ensure that any scientific results shall be published or otherwise made widely available after prior use by the scientists 14 responsible for the experiments. The resulting reduced data shall be the property of the Agency. 3. When placing contracts or entering into agreements, the Agency shall, with regard to the resulting inventions and technical data, secure such rights as may be appropriate for the protection of its interests, of those of the Member States participating in the relevant programme, and of those of persons and bodies under their jurisdiction. These rights shall include in particular the rights of access, of disclosure, and of use. Such inventions and technical data shall be communicated to the participating States. 4. Those inventions and technical data that are th

in particular the rights of access, of disclosure, and of use. Such inventions and technical data shall be communicated to the participating States. 4. Those inventions and technical data that are the property of the Agency shall be disclosed to the Member States and may be used for their own purposes by these Member States and by persons and bodies under their jurisdiction, free of charge. 5. The detailed rules for the application of the foregoing provisions shall be adopted by the Council, by a two-thirds majority of all Member States. 15 Article IV EXCHANGE OF PERSONS Member States shall facilitate the exchange of persons concerned with work within the competence of the Agency, consistent with the application to any person of their laws and regulations relating to entry into, stay in, or departure from, their territories. Article V ACTIVITIES AND PROGRAMMES 1. The activities of the Agency shall include mandatory activities, in which all Member States participate, and optional activities, in which all Member States participate apart from those that formally declare themselves not interested in participating therein. a . With respect to the mandatory activities, the Agency shall: i . ensure the execution of basic activities, such as education, documentation, studies of future projects and technological research work; 16 ii . ensure the elaboration and execution of a scientifi

i . ensure the execution of basic activities, such as education, documentation, studies of future projects and technological research work; 16 ii . ensure the elaboration and execution of a scientific programme including satellites and other space systems; iii . collect relevant information and disseminate it to Member States, draw attention to gaps and duplication, and provide advice and assistance for the harmonisation of international and national programmes; iv . maintain regular contact with the users of space techniques and keep itself informed of their requirements. b . With respect to the optional activities, the Agency shall ensure, in accordance with the provisions of Annex III, the execution of programmes which may, in particular, include: i . the design, development, construction, launching, placing in orbit, and control of satellites and other space systems; ii . the design, development, construction, and operation of launch facilities and space transport systems. 17 2. In the area of space applications the Agency may, should the occasion arise, carry out operational activities under conditions to be defined by the Council by a majority of all Member States. When so doing the Agency shall: a . place at the disposal of the operating agencies concerned such of its own facilities as may be useful to them; b . ensure as required, on behalf of the operating agencies co

oing the Agency shall: a . place at the disposal of the operating agencies concerned such of its own facilities as may be useful to them; b . ensure as required, on behalf of the operating agencies concerned, the launching, placing in orbit and control of operational application satellites; c . carry out any other activity requested by users and approved by the Council. The cost of such operational activities shall be borne by the users concerned. 3. With respect to the coordination and integration of programmes referred to in Article II c , the Agency shall receive in good time from Member States information on projects relating to new space programmes, facilitate consultations among the Member States, undertake any necessary evaluation and formulate appropriate rules to be adopted by the Council by a unanimous vote of all 18 Member States. The objectives and procedures of the internationalisation of programmes are set out in Annex IV. Article VI FACILITIES AND SERVICES 1. For the execution of the programmes entrusted to it, the Agency: a . shall maintain the internal capability required for the preparation and supervision of its tasks and, to this end, shall establish and operate such establishments and facilities as are required for its activities; b . may enter into special arrangements for the execution of certain parts of its programmes by, or in cooperation with, nationa

such establishments and facilities as are required for its activities; b . may enter into special arrangements for the execution of certain parts of its programmes by, or in cooperation with, national institutions of the Member States, or for the management by the Agency itself of certain national facilities. 19 2. In implementing their programmes, the Member States and the Agency shall endeavour to make the best use of their existing facilities and available services as a first priority, and to rationalise them; accordingly they shall not set up new facilities or services without having first examined the possibility of using the existing means. Article VII INDUSTRIAL POLICY 1. The industrial policy which the Agency is to elaborate and apply by virtue of Article II d shall be designed in particular to: a . meet the requirements of the European space programme and the coordinated national space programmes in a cost-effective manner; b . improve the world-wide competitiveness of European industry by maintaining and developing space technology and by encouraging the rationalisation and development of an industrial structure appropriate to market requirements, making use in the first place of the existing industrial potential of all Member States; 20 c . ensure that all Member States participate in an equitable manner, having regard to their financial contribution, in implementin

place of the existing industrial potential of all Member States; 20 c . ensure that all Member States participate in an equitable manner, having regard to their financial contribution, in implementing the European space programme and in the associated development of space technology; in particular the Agency shall, for the execution of its programmes, grant preference to the fullest extent possible to industry in all Member States, which shall be given the maximum opportunity to participate in the work of technological interest undertaken for the Agency; d . exploit the advantages of free competitive bidding in all cases, except where this would be incompatible with other defined objectives of industrial policy. Other objectives may be defined by the Council by a unanimous decision of all Member States. The detailed arrangements for the attainment of these objectives shall be those set out in Annex V and in rules which shall be adopted by the Council by a two-thirds majority of all Member States and reviewed periodically. 21 2. For the execution of its programmes, the Agency shall make the maximum use of external contractors consistent with the maintenance of the internal capability referred to in Article VI, 1. Article VIII LAUNCHERS AND OTHER SPACE TRANSPORT SYSTEMS 1. When defining its missions, the Agency shall take into account the launchers or other space transport syste

ty referred to in Article VI, 1. Article VIII LAUNCHERS AND OTHER SPACE TRANSPORT SYSTEMS 1. When defining its missions, the Agency shall take into account the launchers or other space transport systems developed within the framework of its programmes, or by a Member State, or with a significant Agency contribution, and shall grant preference to their utilisation for appropriate payloads if this does not present an unreasonable disadvantage compared with other launchers or space transport means available at the envisaged time, in respect of cost, reliability and mission suitability. 2. If activities or programmes under Article V include the use of launchers or other space transport systems, the participating States shall, when the programme in question is submitted for approval or acceptance, inform the Council of the launcher or space transport system envisaged. If during 22 the execution of a programme the participating States wish to use a launcher or space transport system other than the one originally adopted, the Council shall make a decision on this change in accordance with the same rules as those applied in respect of the initial approval or acceptance of the programme. Article IX USE OF FACILITIES, ASSISTANCE TO MEMBER STATES, AND SUPPLY OF PRODUCTS 1. Provided that their use for its own activities and programmes is not thereby prejudiced, the Agency shall make its fa

ticle IX USE OF FACILITIES, ASSISTANCE TO MEMBER STATES, AND SUPPLY OF PRODUCTS 1. Provided that their use for its own activities and programmes is not thereby prejudiced, the Agency shall make its facilities available, at the cost of the State concerned, to any Member State that asks to use them for its own programmes. The Council shall determine, by a two-thirds majority of all Member States, the practical arrangements under which the facilities will be made available. 2. If, outside the activities and programmes referred to in Article V but within the purpose of the Agency, one or more Member States wish to engage in a project, the Council may decide by 23 a two-thirds majority of all Member States to make available the assistance of the Agency. The resulting cost to the Agency shall be met by the Member State or States concerned. 3. a . Products developed under a programme of the Agency shall be supplied to any Member State that has taken part in the funding of the programme in question and asks for such products to be supplied for its own purposes. The Council shall determine by a two-thirds majority of all Member States the practical arrangements under which such products will be supplied and in particular the measures to be taken by the Agency in regard to its contractors to enable the requesting Member State to obtain those products. b . This Member State may ask the Ag

l be supplied and in particular the measures to be taken by the Agency in regard to its contractors to enable the requesting Member State to obtain those products. b . This Member State may ask the Agency to state whether it considers that the prices proposed by the contractors are fair and reasonable and whether, under similar circumstances, it would consider them acceptable for the purposes of its own requirements. c . The fulfilment of the requests referred to in this paragraph shall not involve the Agency in any additional costs, and all costs resulting 24 from such requests shall be borne by the requesting Member State. Article X ORGANS The organs of the Agency shall be the Council, and the Director General assisted by a staff. Article XI THE COUNCIL 1. The Council shall be composed of representatives of the Member States. 2. The Council shall meet as and when required, either at delegate level or at ministerial level. The meetings shall be held at the Agency’s Headquarters unless the Council decides otherwise. 3. a . The Council shall elect for two years a Chairman and Vice-chairmen, who may be re-elected once for a further year. The Chairman shall direct the proceedings of the Council and ensure the preparation of its decisions; he shall inform the Member States of proposals for the execution of an optional programme; 25 he shall assist in coordinating the activities of

he Council and ensure the preparation of its decisions; he shall inform the Member States of proposals for the execution of an optional programme; 25 he shall assist in coordinating the activities of the organs of the Agency. He shall maintain liaison with the Member States, through their delegates to the Council, on general policy matters affecting the Agency and shall endeavour to harmonise their views thereon. In the interval between meetings, he shall advise the Director General and shall obtain from him all necessary information. b . The Chairman shall be assisted by a Bureau, the composition of which shall be decided by the Council and which shall be convened by the Chairman. The Bureau shall advise the Chairman in the preparation of Council meetings. 4. When the Council meets at ministerial level it shall elect a chairman for the meeting. The next ministerial meeting shall be convened by him. 5. States; decisions 26 to this effect may only be changed by new decisions adopted by a two-thirds majority of all Member States; ii . determine, by a unanimous decision of all Member States, the level of resources to be made available to the Agency for the coming five-year period; iii . determine, by a unanimous decision of all Member States, towards the end of the third year of each five-year period and after a review of the situation, the level of resources to be made available to the Agency for the new five-year period starting at the end of this third year; b . as regards the activities referred to in Article V, 1 a (iii) and (iv) : i . define the policy to be followed by the Agency in pursuit of its purpose; ii . adopt, by a two-thirds majority of all Member States, recommendations addressed to Member States; c . as regards the optional programmes referred to in Article V, 1 b: 27 i . accept each programme by a majority of all Member States; ii . determine, as appropriate, in the course of their implementation, the order of priority of programmes; d . adopt the annual work plans of the Agency; e . as regards the budgets as defined in Annex II: i . adopt the annual general budget of the Agency by a two-thirds majority of all Member States; ii . adopt each programme budget by a two- thirds majority of the participating States; f . adopt, by a two-thirds majority of all Member

ithin the framework of this Convention. 6. a . Each Member State shall have one vote in the Council. However, a Member State shall not have the right to vote on matters concerning exclusively an accepted programme in which it does not take part. b . A Member State shall have no vote in the Council if the amount of its arrears of 29 contributions to the Agency in respect of all activities and programmes covered by Article V in which it participates exceeds the assessed amount of its contributions for the current financial year. Moreover, if the amount of a Member State’s arrears of contributions to any one of the programmes under Article V, 1 a (ii) or V, 1 b in which it participates exceeds the assessed amount of its contributions to that programme for the current financial year, then that Member State shall have no vote in the Council on questions relating exclusively to that programme. In any such case, the Member State may nevertheless be authorised to vote in the Council if a two-thirds majority of all Member States considers that the non-payment of contributions is due to circumstances beyond its control. c . be necessary to constitute a quorum at any meeting of the Council. d . In determining the unanimity or majorities provided for in this Convention, account shall not be taken of a Member State which has no vote. 7. The Council shall adopt its own rules of procedure. 8. a . The Council shall establish a Science Programme Committee, to which it shall refer any matter relating to the mandatory scientific programme under Article V, 1 a (ii) . The terms of reference of the Science Programme Committee shall be determined by the Council by a two-thirds majority of all Member States and in accordance with this Article. b . The Council may establish such other subordinate bodies as may be necessary for the purpose of the Agency. Article XII DIRECTOR GENERAL AND STAFF 1. a . The Council shall, by a two-thirds majority of all Member States, appoint a Director General for a defined period and may, by the same majority, terminate his appointment. b . The Director General shall be the chief executive officer of the Agency and its legal representative. He shall take all measures necessary for the management of the Agency, the execution of its programmes, the implementation of its policy and the fulfilment of its purpose, in accordance with the directives issued by the Council. He shall have authority over the establishments of the Agency. He shall, in regard to the financial administration of the Agency, act in 32 accordance with the provisions of Annex II. He shall make an annual report to the Council, and this report shall be published. He may also submit proposals concerning activities and programmes as well as measures designed to ensure the fulfilment of the Agency’s purpose. He attends meetings of the Agency without the right to vote. c . The Council may postpone the appointment of the Director General fo

Subsequent Policy and rules shall set forth the specific framework on : 1. Personal Data quality The Policy shall provide data quality conditions, including on accuracy and update of personal data. ons of processing of Personal Data (e.g. collection, recording, disclosure, deletion, etc.) for fair, specified and legitimate purposes, in not excessive manners and in conditions protecting confidentiality, integrity and security o f personal data.
